Birat, J.P. (2012). Sustainability footprint of steelmaking byproducts. Ironmaking and Steelmaking 39(4), 270-277. doi:10.1179/1743281211Y.0000000054

background: Conceptual paper on allocating CO2 between blast furnace hot metal and granulated BF slag sold to cement makers (LCA allocation, system expansion, consequential LCA). It prints no technology-level energy use, cost, capacity, capture rate or TRL; in particular nothing on top-gas recycling, CCS or CCS costs, so it does not support the IPCC AR6 Table 11.3 row (BF-BOF with TGR and CCU/S, 60%, USD70-130/t) that cites it in footnote a. What it has: Table 1 (p.273): illustrative mill 4 Mt/yr crude steel at 2.11 t CO2/t steel; 250 kg BF slag/t hot metal; clinker 0.78-0.91 t CO2/t (0.51 from limestone calcination; 0.28/0.35/0.40 from oil/coal/coke firing); slag CO2 allocations 1.24, 0.54, 1.72 and 0.01 t CO2/t slag by method; synergy saves 0.24 t CO2/t steel or 0.64 t CO2/t cement; steelmaking slag 300-400 kg/t steel (p.272). Locators are printed journal pages 270-277.
